purpose: Test a precise fresh-source noncancellation lemma, rather than recompute large ranks
candidate: For the actual single seed, whenever H_n=(c(i+j))_(i,j<n) is invertible and the newest nonlinear source c(2n-1)*cell(2n-1,1) is one, its bordered Schur pivot epsilon_n is one
reason_to_test: The newest source occurs in c(2n), not in any prior matrix entry; this is a direct candidate interpretation of an uncancelled source creating a Hankel pivot. Earlier source contributions can still cancel it, which must be checked rather than assumed.
exact_pivot: epsilon_n=c(2n)+u^T H_n^(-1)u, u_i=c(n+i); over F2 the quadratic form equals diag(H_n^(-1)) dot u
falsifier: An actual-seed n with invertible H_n, newest source one, and epsilon_n zero
verification: Exact GF2 elimination, literal Rule30 rows; separate Rule150 Duhamel decomposition for the first counterexample and an independent Wolfram CellularAutomaton check
scope: Counterexamples reject this precise candidate, not every source-based rank-growth mechanism; a positive finite range does not prove an all-n lemma
